title: Deleting an untouched contracted point blowup from a surface tower
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0$ be a finite tower of $S$-morphisms between integral regular Noetherian schemes of dimension two [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Each $b_i$ is the blowup of a reduced closed point $x_{i-1}\in X_{i-1}$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X_{i-1},x_{i-1}}=2$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Fix $1\le a\le n$. Put $E_a=b_a^{-1}(x_{a-1})$ and let $E_i\subset X_i$ for $i>a$ be its successive strict transforms [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Assume $x_{i-1}\notin E_{i-1}$ for every $i>a$. Let $Z$ be an $S$-scheme and $f:X_n\to Z$ an $S$-morphism whose topological image $f(E_n)$ consists of one point. Then there are a tower $p':X'_{n-1}\to X_0$ of $n-1$ reduced-closed-point blowups between integral regular Noetherian surfaces, an $S$-morphism $c:X_n\to X'_{n-1}$, and an $S$-morphism $f':X'_{n-1}\to Z$, such that $p'c=b_1\cdots b_n$ and $f'c=f$. The morphism $c$ is itself the blowup of a reduced closed point, its exceptional fibre is $E_n$, and it is an isomorphism away from that fibre. If $V\subset X_0$ is open and every original centre maps outside $V$, every centre of $p'$ also maps outside $V$, and these maps identify with the original identity maps over $V$.

proof.text: Put $Y_{a-1}=X_{a-1}$ and $c_a=b_a:X_a\to Y_{a-1}$, with centre $z_a=x_{a-1}$. We inductively construct $Y_{i-1}\to\cdots\to Y_{a-1}$ and a point blowup $c_i:X_i\to Y_{i-1}$ with centre $z_i$ of local dimension two, exceptional fibre $E_i$, and $c_i$ an isomorphism off $E_i$. The square with the original composite to $X_{a-1}$ must commute. These requirements hold for $i=a$ by the hypotheses and the complement isomorphism. The schemes $Y_{i-1}$ will be integral regular Noetherian surfaces. If $a=n$, there are no induction steps.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), part (1); initialization of the tower induction

proof.text:
Suppose $a\le i<n$ and the induction data are constructed. Write $T=Y_{i-1}$, $z=z_i$, $q=x_i$, and $y=c_i(q)$. The hypothesis $q
otin E_i$ and the complement isomorphism give $y
e z$ and identify the local rings at $q$ and $y$. Thus $\dim\mathcal O_{T,y}=2$. The point $y$ is closed: $\{q\}$ is closed in $X_i$ and $c_i$ is proper by regular point-blowup geometry, hence closed by the definition of properness. Let $d_i:Y_i=\operatorname{Bl}_yT	o T$. The same geometry gives integrality, regularity, Noetherianity and the complement isomorphism for $Y_i$. It also gives local dimension two at its closed exceptional points; elsewhere the local rings are those of $T$. Consequently $\dim Y_i\le2$: any finite chain of specializations extends to a closed point in a Noetherian space, and is bounded by that local dimension. The closed point $z$ has a unique preimage $z'\in Y_i$ because $z
e y$; its local ring is $\mathcal O_{T,z}$, of dimension two. Therefore $\dim Y_i=2$ and $z'$ is a reduced closed point of local dimension two.

source.place: Tags 0AGR (lemma-blowup-regular), 0AGQ (lemma-blowup); closedness and local dimensions in the induction

proof.text: Form $B=\operatorname{Bl}_{z'}Y_i$. Compare $X_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_qX_i$ with $B$ over $T$ on the open cover $U=T\setminus\{y\}$, $W=T\setminus\{z\}$. Flat blowup base change applies to these open inclusions: their maps on local rings are isomorphisms and hence flat. Over $U$, the $q$-blowup is the identity, $d_i$ is the identity, and the $z'$-blowup is the $z$-blowup; thus both restrictions are canonically $\operatorname{Bl}_zU$. Over $W$, $c_i$ is the identity, $q$ is the reduced point $y$ under that identity, and the $z'$-blowup is the identity; thus both restrictions are canonically $\operatorname{Bl}_yW$. Here centres and their ideals are identified scheme-theoretically by these isomorphisms, not merely by their supports. Over $U\cap W$ every blowup is the complement isomorphism. The two local identifications and their inverses therefore agree there, as the identity over $U\cap W$. Glue the maps to $B$ and the inverse maps to $X_{i+1}$ by scheme-morphism gluing; their composites are identities on each covering open, hence globally. This gives an isomorphism $h_i:X_{i+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ over $T$. Define $c_{i+1}$ as $h_i$ followed by the blowup $B\to Y_i$. Then $d_ic_{i+1}=c_ib_{i+1}$, since this equality holds on both opens.

source.place: Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), restricted to the two complementary opens; Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), part (1)

proof.text: The fibre of $c_{i+1}$ above $z'$ lies over $U$ and there is exactly $c_i^{-1}(z)=E_i$, viewed in $X_{i+1}$ by the isomorphism away from $q$. This is $E_{i+1}$ as a closed subscheme: $E_i$ is disjoint from the centre $q$, its inverse image is closed, and that entire inverse image is already in the open used in the definition of strict transform, so taking its scheme-theoretic closure adds nothing. Thus $c_{i+1}$ has exceptional fibre $E_{i+1}$ and is an isomorphism off it. The point $z'$ has local dimension two by step 2, so all induction requirements hold at $i+1$. Repeat for $i=a,\ldots,n-1$. Concatenate the unchanged first $a-1$ blowups with $d_a,\ldots,d_{n-1}$. This is a tower $p':Y_{n-1}\to X_0$ of $(a-1)+(n-a)=n-1$ point blowups of the required surfaces. Set $c=c_n$. The commuting squares, composed, give $p'c=b_1\cdots b_n$. In the case $n=a=1$, $p'$ is the empty tower and $c=b_1$.

source.place: Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), two-open construction; strict-transform definition for a disjoint centre

proof.text: Apply point-blowdown factorization to $c:X_n\to Y_{n-1}$ and $f$. Its base is regular Noetherian of dimension two by the induction, its centre is a reduced closed point, and its exceptional fibre is $E_n$ with singleton image under $f$. It supplies a unique scheme morphism $f':Y_{n-1}\to Z$ with $f'c=f$. This map is over $S$: writing $s_Z,s_Y,s_X$ for the structure morphisms, both $s_Zf'$ and $s_Y$ become $s_X$ after composition with $c$. They are equal by the uniqueness clause of the same point-blowdown factorization, applied now to $s_X:X_n\to S$. This application is valid because $s_X=s_Yc$ has singleton image on the nonempty fibre $E_n$. All constructed maps to $Y_i$ and $X_0$ are already over $S$, by their construction over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0C5J (lemma-factor-through-contraction), existence and uniqueness; apply uniqueness also to the structure map

proof.text: Finally suppose all original centres map outside $V\subset X_0$. Every retained old centre has its original image. Each new centre in step 2 is $y=c_i(x_i)$, so the commuting square makes its image in $X_0$ exactly the original image of $x_i$. The moved centre $z'$ maps to $z$, and recursively to $x_{a-1}$. Hence every centre of $p'$ and of $c$ maps outside $V$. The complement isomorphism identifies each old and new blowup restriction over $V$ with the identity on $V$. The local identifications used in step 3 restrict there to the identity too (over either member of the two-open cover); scheme-morphism gluing makes these restrictions agree globally. Composing these identifications proves the claimed compatibility over $V$.
